intended_object: The inclusion SL_n ⊆ GL_n restricted to the first-order identity fibers: the group homomorphism from ker(SL_n(R[ε]) → SL_n(R)) to ker(GL_n(R[ε]) → GL_n(R)), where R[ε] is the ring of dual numbers and both maps reduce modulo ε. Inferred from the docstring and from the module documentation.
explanation:
`slReduce` and `glReduce` are `Matrix.SpecialLinearGroup.map` and `Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup.map` applied to `DualNumber.fstRingHom R`, so their kernels are the identity fibers of reduction mod ε. The function sends an element g of the SL kernel to `Matrix.SpecialLinearGroup.toGL g`. The proof `slKernel_fst` shows that the image lies in the GL kernel: its first component is the identity matrix. The map is multiplicative because `toGL` is a group homomorphism, so the definition is exactly the restriction of the SL→GL inclusion to these kernels, as the docstring says.

On generality: the same restriction would work for any ring homomorphism, not only for reduction of dual numbers. But this map is an auxiliary piece of a module about dual-number kernels. It feeds `slReadback` and `slKerEquiv`, which identify the SL kernel with the trace-zero matrices sl_n(R). There, R is already an arbitrary commutative ring and n an arbitrary finite type with decidable equality, so it is not too narrow. Mathlib has no ready-made counterpart for this restricted map; in principle one could build it from `MonoidHom.restrict` and `codRestrict`.
